text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A scandal has broken out over a deal worth $3.9 million between the Latvian defence ministry and Slovak company Katrim Stella, which was to supply Latvia with infantry weapons. The weapons which the company delivered turned out to be used ones. Latvia's security police is investigating the case. Former prime minister Maris Gailis, who was also defence minister, denies any responsibility for the deal.

- Parliament ratified at the second and final reading the agreement on free trade in agricultural products between Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania. The agreement was approved by 55 votes against four and eight abstentions.
- The chairman of the Latvian Social-Democratic Workers Party said it is not ready to admit former finance minister Aivars Kreituss and wife Ilga Kreituse to its ranks.

- The security police arrested Gatis Kruze, one of the alleged main figures in the scandal of Lata International, a company which received one sixth of Latvia's foreign credits to support farming agriculture at the time of former prime minister Ivars Godmanis and squandered them.
- The Russian foreign ministry issued a statement saying Russia may carry out a unilateral delimitation of its border with Latvia if the Latvian side continues to hold up talks.
- The cabinet wants to bring forward the expiry date of privatisation vouchers as well as to reduce their value. The question is to be considered at next week's cabinet meeting.
- Latvia's general prosecutor's office and security police are investigating the involvement of the state revenue service in fuel contraband.

- MP Maris Vitols (24) has been appointed parliamentary secretary of the finance ministry. He will hold the office while the functions of the finance minister are fulfilled by Prime Minister Andris Shkele.
- A toxic and dangerous waste storage facility has been completed in the territory of a former Soviet tank base at Gardene, near Dobele.

- According to a competent source in the Latvian parliament, the procedure to ratify the licence agreement between Latvia and companies AMOCO and Swedish OPAB is almost sure to be started next week, when the licence agreement will be considered at the first reading. The agreement is the main cause of argument between Lithuania and Latvia in a sea border dispute.
